subject: POC scaling plan & success checklist — BrightEdge
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia@brightedge.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:05:00 -0500
Subject: POC scaling plan & success checklist — BrightEdge

Thanks for the call earlier — great to meet the BrightEdge team. Summary + proposed next steps below so we have one source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Quick recap of goals (as discussed):
- Validate inference quality and integration with BrightEdge ranking pipeline for re-ranking use case.
- Confirm production latency SLOs (p95 < 150ms) and cost envelope for 50k monthly queries in steady state.
- Exercise autoscaling and burst behavior during report generation windows.

Proposed success criteria (short list):
1) Accuracy: parity to current baseline on the provided eval set (>=95% of baseline NDCG on the test set in sheet 'eval_scores').
2) Latency: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn requests at 95th percentile traffic pattern.
3) Throughput: steady-state handle 80 qps with tail latency target; support bursts to 300 qps for short windows (<=10m) without failures.
4) Cost: predicted per-query cost within the threshold we discussed (we'll provide an estimate once capacity is finalized).

POC scope & timeline (proposed):
- Feb 1: provision trial (sandbox) environment and exchange test credentials.
- Feb 2–7: ingest sample indexing slices, run baseline comparisons, and run smoke load tests.
- Feb 8–14: 2-week evaluation with traffic replay + 2 scheduled simulated burst periods.
- Feb 15: wrap + calibration call to review results and next steps.

Capacity ask (initial):
- Reserved pool: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool for consistent KV cache behavior.
- Autoscale policy: min=1 GPU, target steady=2 GPUs, scale-up steps to a max of 6 GPUs during sustained high load.
- Burst/ephemeral: allow ephemeral burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) up to additional 4 GPUs for short windows (<=10 minutes) to emulate report-time spikes.

Owners / contacts:
- Redwood: Karthik (sales, overall lead), Vanessa (solutions engineer — infra + tuning), Marissa (CS — onboarding and success metrics).
- BrightEdge: Lydia (POC owner), Samir (infra/engineering).

Attachments: BrightEdge_POC_requirements.xlsx (sample eval set + integration notes), redwood-poc-template.pdf (POC checklist).

Next steps:
- Lydia/Samir: confirm the two-week window and peak burst requirement (you mentioned bursts during ETL runs — please confirm expected duration/frequency).
- Redwood: we will draft a short MOU + provisioning plan and share a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly what we needed, clear and actionable. A couple clarifications from our side:  

- Burst pattern: we typically see 3–4 short spikes per day during report generation, each ~5–8 minutes long, where traffic jumps to ~250–350 qps. That aligns with your proposed ephemeral burst capacity, but we want to make sure the scaling latency doesn't cause errors during the ramp.
- Throughput baseline: steady-state for our trial should be treated as 60–90 qps depending on replay slices; the 80 qps target is fine.
- Data: we'll provide a 72-hour sample traffic replay and a static eval set (see BrightEdge_POC_requirements.xlsx sheet 'traffic').

One ask on pricing: can you provide a rough committed cost for the reserved 2-GPU pool + expected ephemeral usage for the 2-week trial? We need this to get fast approval from procurement.

If you can send an MOU and a Link to DocuSign, we'll have Samir confirm internal sign-off by Monday.

Best,
Lydia
Head of Search Products, BrightEdge Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 18:00:00 -0500
Subject: RE: POC scaling plan & success checklist — BrightEdge (capacity notes)

Internal notes / sizing recommendations after the call:  

- GPU types: recommend H100-equivalent for best latency per cost on large-context ranking models; A100 class is acceptable if customer has constraints. For trial keep option configurable.
- Baseline sizing: reserve 2 GPUs (dedicated pool) to ensure consistent KV cache residency and warm startup behaviour. This matches Karthik's ask.
- Autoscale rules: min=1, steady target=2, scale steps: +1 GPU per 30s of sustained CPU/GPU utilization >70% up to max=6. Cooler-down: scale-down when utilization <40% for 90s.
- Burst handling: use ephemeral pool for instant additional capacity — recommend setting ephemeral burst cap at +4 GPUs to reliably reach 300–350 qps during 5–8 minute spikes. Ephemeral should be billed separately and capped in the MOU.
- Load testing plan: run 3 replay windows during the 2-week trial — one steady 3-hour run, two 10-minute burst tests at 250 qps and 320 qps. Capture p50/p95/p99 and error rates; include token-level cost breakdown.
- Observability: enable tracing and per-request token cost on the trial API key; retain logs for 30 days.

I'll draft a short infra appendix for the MOU listing these params. Also will include runbook steps for 'scale-failure' and an SLA fallback: auto-failover to a smaller model variant for 2 minutes to avoid 5xxs during scale windows.

—Vanessa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Lydia. Confirming next steps and a couple of concrete items so procurement can proceed:  

1) MOU & pricing: we'll put together a 2-week trial MOU that covers:
   - Reserved 2x GPU pool (choice of H100 or A100) for the trial period.
   - Ephemeral burst up to +4 GPUs (metered).
   - Estimated bill: Reserved GPU flat fee + ephemeral estimated consumption. I'll include a conservative cost estimate in the MOU and a line-item for overage.
2) Kickoff & credentials: propose provisioning on Feb 1 morning (ET). Please confirm and we'll send service account credentials + test keys by Jan 29.
3) Tests & schedule: we'll run the three load windows Vanessa suggested. We'll provide a small test harness for replay that integrates with your traffic dump.
4) Approval ask for you: confirm the burst frequency/duration (your call said 3–4 spikes/day, ~5–8m each) and confirm procurement wants an explicit hard cap on ephemeral spend.

I'll attach the draft MOU and the infra appendix once Vanessa finishes the appendix (end of day). If all looks good I'll send the DocuSign link by Friday.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.
Karthik
